title: Mitigate signal-sparsity-trigger-misfires-and-warm-pool-provisioning-playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a recent capacity incident on 2026-02-27 we observed repeated autoscaler misfires where KEDA/HPA failed to provision warm-pool capacity for short, bursty traffic patterns. Root causes included sparse event signals (long idle tails), a stale KEDA trigger window, and request coalescing at the proxy layer hiding load from scaler metrics. This ticket tracks the postmortem findings, proposed mitigations, and an operational playbook for preventing recurrence and reducing mean time to recovery for similar events.
timeline: 2026-02-27 03:12 UTC: Pager triggered for elevated 95th latency in text-gen region-us-west1; initial mitigation by increasing replica target via emergency runbook.
2026-02-27 03:45 UTC: Manual warm-pool resize restored tail latency; investigation started; KEDA logs show few trigger events in preceding 10m windows.
2026-02-27 08:00 UTC: Incident conference call, on-call noted proxy request coalescing (burst bundling) causing metric sparsity seen by KEDA scaler.
2026-03-01: Postmortem investigation kickoff; reproduced locally with traffic replayer; confirmed metric sparsity plus KEDA window too coarse and HPA reaction hysteresis insufficient.
2026-03-04: Spike test shows KEDA misses for bursts <6s when proxy bundles requests into 1s aggregated metrics; KV cache hit-rate changes also mask real compute demand.
2026-03-09: Proposal reviewed with SRE and Runtime teams; agreed on three-pronged mitigation: synthetic probe, dynamic trigger window, and probe gating/aggregation hygiene.
2026-03-10: This ticket opened to implement mitigations and runbook updates; staging tests are passing for synthetic probe and adjusted KEDA config.
comments: 2026-03-02 Marco Nguyen: Initial repro attached (link to traffic replayer) and KEDA logs; reproduces 80% of scenarios when bundling enabled.
2026-03-03 Priya Rao (SRE): Observed that our metric pipeline aggregates at 1s which loses short bursts; suggested emitting a synthetic 'probe' metric at the pod to indicate readiness/load.

2026-03-05 Dylan Chen (Runtime): Kernel scheduling improved but does not change trigger visibility; recommended adjusting KEDA polling and adding a 95th-percentile smoothing window instead of simple moving average.
2026-03-06 Product review: PMs approved playbook but requested an experiment gating logic to avoid overprovisioning during low-utilization maintenance windows.
2026-03-09 Aisha Patel: Added list of action items and owners below. Confirmed that two staging PRs exist for probe exporter and KEDA config change.
2026-03-10 Marco Nguyen: Opening follow-up tickets for dashboard alerts and runbook PR; added link to the canary test plan.

postmortem_summary: Root causes: (1) metric sparsity from proxy-level request coalescing; (2) KEDA trigger windows and polling frequency tuned for longer-running steady traffic, not short bursts; (3) HPA hysteresis thresholds insufficient when combined with warm-pool sizing, causing slow ramp and tail latency. Impact: medium (tail latency degradation and short customer errors during 12-minute window). Agreed mitigations balance sensitivity vs cost: emit probe metrics to surface bursts, tighten KEDA responsiveness with percentile smoothing, and update proxy aggregation hygiene to avoid hiding events.
acceptance_criteria: Staging canary shows KEDA scales within target SLO for 80% of 1-6s bursts without increasing baseline capacity.
Dashboards alert when bundling ratio >20% and scaler misses are detected.
Runbook updated with step-by-step manual resize and automated fallback play for warm-pool failures.
Two independent region canaries completed and verified by SRE and Runtime leads.
